page.layout: One page of text in a single column; a margin note at the left edge beside the verse section ("Prosphonesis ad Romam"); a catchword-like word "vere" at the lower right; running head at the top.

main_text.p: & ima viscera Ecclesiæ arrodentium, molem עת רעה tempus malum Amos. v. 13. & Καιρὸς χαλεπὸς tempora difficilia 2 Timoth. iii. 1. dixeris merito. Exiverunt pridem, exeúntque quotidie ex portis Ecclesiæ hujus seductores Spiritus ad Reges terræ & habitabilis totius, ut eos congregent ad prœlium diei illius magnæ Dei Omnipotentis in locum Harmageddon Hebraicè dictum. Ecce, ita interea Filius Dei ex Cœlo fideles suos alloquitur, venio sicut fur. Beatus qui vigilat, & custodit vestimenta sua, ne nudus ambulet, & videant turpitudinem ejus, Apoc. xvi. 14–17.
main_text.head: CCCL. Tu verò ROMA,

l.i: Nec Roma Romæ compos, sed tamen Roma,
Sed Roma, quæ præstare non potes Romam,
Sed quæ foveris fraude, quæ foves fraudem.
Te prostituta vincis, & tuum facta es

main_text.p: Tu omnium in Christiano Orbe malorum causa es, quorum tibi coram Deo forti, justo, Zelote reddenda erit quandoque ratio. Propter te mactantur, affliguntur, vexantur tot millia hominum Christum Salvatorem suum ve-rè

page.notes: Hebrew word "רעה" (עת רעה) in the first line; Greek "Καιρὸς χαλεπὸς" as printed. Left margin note is "Prosphonesis ad Romam" (set in small italic, split over two lines in print). The final word "verè" is split at the line end and continues on the next page.
